messages:
amy_support: ACME reporting a big vectors/sec regression after the midnight routing change. tokens/sec stable, no 5xxs, just long tails on embeddings. Can someone triage?
acme_ops: Confirmed. Started ~00:58 UTC. Vectors/sec ~30% of baseline, tokens/sec steady. Payloads typically 512-dim; client lib now sending X-vec-dim:2048 header. Batches vary 8-32.
maya: Any routing/model variant rollouts at ~00:55? @rebecca
rebecca: We rolled a small routing optimization at 00:55 to prefer cost-optimized variants for unpinned customers. ACME should be pinned, but suspect a tag mismatch — investigating.
dmitri: Metrics: cluster-7 embed queue depth jumped 40 -> 580 at 00:59. GPU utilization steady ~65%. Per-request CPU time spiked on embed runtime nodes.
ops-bot: alert: embeddings.queue.depth spike on cluster-7 (00:59 UTC) value=580
amy_support: Could this be a dim mismatch causing CPU reshape/slow path and disabling fast batching?
dmitri: Logs show repeated lines: "dim_mismatch: client_dim=2048 catalog_dim=512 -> cpu_fallback" and then "batching: cannot_batch cpu_fallback". Sample:
2026-10-15T00:59:12Z [warn] request_id=abc dim_mismatch client_dim=2048 catalog_dim=512 path=cpu_fallback
2026-10-15T00:59:13Z [warn] request_id=abc batching: cannot_batch cpu_fallback
acme_ops: We deployed client lib v2.3.4 around 00:50 that added an X-vec-dim header by mistake. Rolling back now.
maya: Short-term mitigation: force-route ACME to verified openembed-512 for their traffic. I'll patch routing rule for customer:acme.
rebecca: Applying routing override to cluster-7 now.
ops-bot: deploy: routing override applied customer=acme -> model=openembed-512 on cluster-7
acme_ops: Vectors/sec recovering, back to near-normal within ~90s. Thanks.
amy_support: Let's capture repro steps and a short runbook for support KB.
maya: Repro + triage commands:
1) repro curl (adds header):
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
 -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" \
 -H "X-vec-dim: 2048" \
 -d '{"model":"openembed-xl","input":["test"]}'
2) check runtime logs:
 kubectl logs -f deploy/embed-runtime | grep dim_mismatch
3) check queue depth metric:
 curl http://metrics.cluster-7.internal/queues/embed-vectors | jq .length
4) inspect routing for customer:
 curl -s http://control-plane.internal/routing?customer=acme
Runbook summary: If vectors/sec drop while tokens/sec stable -> check for dim_mismatch logs -> check per-customer routing/model pin -> apply temporary routing override to compatible model -> advise customer to remove header/rollback client -> create runtime issue for early-reject.
dmitri: Filed RUNTIME-1439: add early-reject on unexpected client vector-dim and per-customer dim_mismatch metric. Assigned eng-runtime.
rebecca: Adding a short-term grafana alert for per-customer dim_mismatch spikes.
amy_support: ACME confirms SLA restored. Logging notes in the support ticket and monitoring RUNTIME-1439 for progress. Closing thread unless more follows.
ops-bot: ticket created RUNTIME-1439
